title: Word problems
lines: Word problems test translation more than mathematics. Turn each sentence into an equation, label units, and check that your answer makes sense in the story. When the algebra looks long, back-solve from the answer choices.
## Translating words into algebra
- "is" means =; "of" usually means multiply; "more than" adds; "less than" subtracts in reverse order: "5 less than x" is x − 5.
- Name each unknown with a letter that reminds you what it is (t for time, c for cost).
- Write units next to numbers; mixing minutes and hours is a leading cause of wrong answers.
## Rates and speed
- Distance = rate × time. Rate = distance ÷ time.
- Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. It is not the average of the speeds unless equal times are spent at each speed.
- Moving toward each other, speeds add; moving the same way, subtract the slower from the faster.
> Chen drives 60 km to a lake at 40 km/h and returns the same 60 km at 60 km/h. What is his average speed?
> Time out = 60/40 = 1.5 h; time back = 60/60 = 1 h.
> Average speed = 120 km ÷ 2.5 h = 48 km/h, not (40 + 60)/2 = 50.
> Two trains 300 km apart travel toward each other at 70 km/h and 80 km/h. When do they meet?
> Closing speed = 150 km/h, so time = 300 ÷ 150 = 2 hours.
! Equal distances at two speeds always give an average below the simple mean, because more time is spent at the slower speed.
## Work problems
- Convert each worker to a rate: a job done in t hours means 1/t of the job per hour.
- Rates add when people work together: 1/a + 1/b = 1/T. A drain or a worker undoing the job subtracts.
- For two workers the together-time is ab/(a + b).
> Priya can paint a room in 6 hours and Mateo in 3 hours. How long working together?
> Rates: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 1/2 room per hour, so 2 hours.
> A pipe fills a tank in 4 hours; a leak empties a full tank in 12 hours. With both open, how long to fill it?
> Net rate = 1/4 − 1/12 = 3/12 − 1/12 = 1/6 tank per hour, so 6 hours.
! The together-time must be less than the fastest worker's time alone. An answer of 4.5 hours (the average of 6 and 3) is impossible.
## Mixtures
- Track the amount of the ingredient, not the percent: amount = concentration × volume.
- Weighted average shortcut: the final concentration sits between the two, closer to the larger quantity. The quantities are in the inverse ratio of the distances.
> How many liters of 60% acid must be added to 20 L of 30% acid to make a 40% mixture?
> Shortcut: 40 is 10 from 30 and 20 from 60, so the volumes are in ratio 20 : 10 = 2 : 1. Half of 20 L is 10 L.
## Simple and compound interest
- Simple interest: I = P × r × t, earned only on the original principal.
- Compound interest: A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿᵗ, where n is the number of compounding periods per year.
- Compound always beats simple over more than one period at the same rate.
> Olga invests $2,000 at 5% per year for 3 years. Compare simple and annual compound interest.
> What does $1,000 grow to in one year at 8% per year compounded quarterly?
! In compound questions with 3 or more periods, use the on-screen calculator; estimating 1.05³ as 1.15 is too rough when choices differ by a few dollars.
## Profit, cost and discounts
- Profit = revenue − cost. Profit percent is normally measured against cost.
- Markups are percents of cost; discounts are percents of the marked price. These are different bases.
> A shop buys a lamp for $40, marks it up 50%, then sells it at 20% off the marked price. What is the profit as a percent of cost?
> Marked price = 40 × 1.5 = $60. Sale price = 60 × 0.8 = $48.
> Profit = 48 − 40 = $8, which is 8/40 = 20% of cost.
! Up 50% and down 20% is not up 30%: the factors multiply, 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2.
## Age problems
- Use one variable for each person's age now. "In k years" adds k to everyone; "k years ago" subtracts k from everyone.
> Amara is three times as old as Kwame. In 10 years she will be twice as old as he is. How old is each now?
> Let Kwame be k, Amara 3k. In 10 years: 3k + 10 = 2(k + 10).
> 3k + 10 = 2k + 20, so k = 10. Kwame is 10 and Amara 30. Check: 40 = 2 × 20.
## Sequences
- Arithmetic (constant difference d): aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d. Sum of the first n terms = n(a₁ + aₙ)/2.
- Geometric (constant ratio r): aₙ = a₁ × rⁿ⁻¹.
- Recursive rules define each term from the one before; write out terms until you see the pattern.
> In 5, 8, 11, …, find the 40th term and the sum of the first 40 terms.
> a₁ = 3 and aₙ = 2aₙ₋₁ − 1. Find a₅.
! The nth term uses n − 1 steps, not n. The 40th term is 39 differences after the first.
## Unit conversion
- Multiply by fractions equal to 1, such as (1,000 m)/(1 km), so that unwanted units cancel.
- Squared and cubed units convert with the square or cube: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 10,000 cm² and 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³.
> Convert 72 km/h to meters per second.
> A floor of 3 m² is how many cm²?
## Strategy
- Back-solve whenever the choices are numbers: plug a choice into the story and see whether every condition holds.
- Sanity-check: a time cannot be negative, a discount price must be lower, a mixture's concentration lies between its parts.
- Word problems take time. If you have read it twice and still cannot set it up, mark it, guess, and return later.
